Iris K.: Throwing an idea on the board: 'consent-first bursting slices' to avoid cross-region failovers during spikes while respecting tenant residency.
Rahul Patel: Explain 'consent-first' quickly?
Iris K.: Each tenant has a residency flag: REGION_ONLY or REGION_PREFERRED (consent). For REGION_PREFERRED we allow best-effort routing to global burst pool; for REGION_ONLY we never route out.
Jordan Lee: How is burst pool sized? Static or adaptive? If adaptive, how do we avoid thrash causing eviction storms across regions?
Iris K.: Proposal: keep two numbers per region: guaranteed_resident_capacity and burst_capacity. Burst_capacity is globally fungible but subject to per-tenant consent. Also a cooldown window per preemption to avoid oscillation (e.g., 60s).
Rahul Patel: Eviction semantics matter. If we yank a running job in us-west to free burst capacity for an EU resident, we need safe handoff. Can't just SIGTERM.
Jordan Lee: Agreed. Add a state: PREEMPT_PENDING. Worker signals `preempt_request` to running task; task returns `preempt_safe_marker` when at a safe checkpoint. After timeout, we cancel.
ops-bot: Alert rule: preemptions.p90_time > 30s => page #eng-sre.
Iris K.: For KV-heavy tasks (kv_owner=true) disallow hard preempt unless lease token transferred. We can implement a lightweight lease token exchange API: `POST /leases/transfer` returning transfer_token and estimated_handoff_ms.
Rahul Patel: Also need proxy-level consent header so routing can prefer local slice. Something like `X-Tenant-Consent: region_only|preferred`. Proxy reads tenant metadata cache.
Jordan Lee: Routing policy sketch: priority order: 1) region-only -> local guaranteed. 2) preferred + local capacity -> local. 3) preferred + no local -> shared burst (if consent). 4) fallback -> queue or degrade.
Iris K.: Telemetry: burst.allocations_by_tenant, burst.preemptions, preemptions.kv_conflicts, and burst.saturation_by_region. Dashboards will make tuning easier.
Rahul Patel: One more safety: add a max_preempt_per_min per region to bound blast radius. Also make it a runtime knob we can dial down during incidents.
Jordan Lee: I can prototype the handshake state machine and lease-transfer API. Iris, can you draft a tiny perf test (synthetic hotspots across two regions) so we can validate tail latency impact?
Iris K.: Yep, I'll write a quick perf plan and stub configs. Rahul, can you add the proxy header + tenant metadata flag?
Rahul Patel: On it. I'll also add unit tests verifying region_only never leaves region.
ops-bot: Deploy: consent-burst-v0.2 canary in eu-west-1 (10%) - logs: "burst:allocated tenant=acme corp region=eu-west-1
Iris K.: Thanks. If this works we avoid many noisy cross-region failovers and give customers a clear consent contract. Follow-up in 48h with results. :thumbsup:"
